Label of this patch text, given on a record that is not in the data package (pass 1, confirmed by execution in the second verification): always applies repair() (clamping to [0,1]) in repairAndDecode, dropping the developer's 'boundaries != null' guard. For unbounded problems decode() is the identity, so the returned optimum point is clamped to [0,1] in every coordinate - a regression the tests miss because their unbounded optima lie at 0 or 1. Executed (JDK 21): the trigger test passes with the patch, and every relevant test that passes with the developer fix passes with it; unbounded CMA-ES on (x-5)^2+(y+3)^2 returns (5,-3) with the developer fix and the buggy version, (1.0, 0.0) with the patch.

Label of this patch text, given on a record that is not in the data package (pass 1, confirmed by execution in the second verification): removes the double time-zone offset by taking the year of instantMillis, but in the formatter-selected chronology instead of the instant's own chronology as the developer does. When the formatter overrides the zone (withZone), the default year is computed in that zone while the local fields come from the instant's zone, so near a year boundary the wrong default year still occurs. Executed (JDK 21): the trigger tests pass with the patch, and every relevant test that passes with the developer fix passes with it; a formatter withZone(UTC) parsing "2 29" into a 2004-12-31T20:00 New York instant gives 2004-02-29T20:00Z with the developer fix and the buggy version, and the patch throws IllegalFieldValueException (dayOfMonth 29). (With a Buddhist chronology override the patch is right where the developer fix throws.)
